The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has uncovered a gun manufacturing factory in Kaduna State, recovering finished firearms and materials used for the production of weapons. The discovery was made during a raid by NDLEA operatives in the Sabon Garin Kangin area of the state, where the owner of the factory was also arrested. The agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement shared on his X handle on Sunday. According to Babafemi, the operation led to the recovery of completed firearms and materials intended for the production of additional weapons. The statement said, “In the course of a raid operation by @ndlea_nigeria officers in Sabon Garin Kangin area of Kaduna some days ago, they discovered a gun factory where finished firearms and materials for the production of more weapons were recovered, and the owner was arrested.” He noted that the discovery further highlighted the connection between drug trafficking, substance abuse and other forms of criminal activities. “This reinforces the fact that there’s a nexus between substance abuse, drug trafficking and other forms of crime,” he said. Similarly, a statement by Babafemi on Sunday added that the NDLEA also intercepted a 25.05-kilogram consignment of methamphetamine concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa through the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, Lagos State. Babafemi disclosed that the trafficker, whose real name is Chinedu Onwude, was arrested on Wednesday at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “The meth suspect, Omokan Isaac Babatope, whose real name is Chinedu Onwude, was arrested on Wednesday, 11th November 2026, at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine, with a total weight of 25.05kg. “The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening,” the statement partly read. According to the statement, Onwude had lived in South Africa for more than 24 years and held both Nigerian and South African passports. “The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years. In another operation, the anti-narcotics agency arrested an American citizen, Greene Khiree, with a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand. “Also, on Wednesday, 11th November, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen, Greene Da’monte Khiree, who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai. “The suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage. He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park. “A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms. A tracking device was also recovered from the bags. “The suspect, a native of Savannah, Georgia, USA, who claimed he had lived in Thailand since October 2025, where he plays professional basketball, said he came to Nigeria on holiday to build networks for his basketball career. “A forensic examination of his mobile phone revealed information pointing to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity,” the statement read. Among other successful operations nationwide, NDLEA operatives on Tuesday arrested a 33-year-old man, Taiwo Aderoju, in an intelligence-led operation at Ebute Metta, where 119.71kg of cannabis sativa was recovered from him. The NDLEA added that officers on patrol at Jere, along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, on Friday, intercepted a 31-year-old woman, Tabara Dauda, conveying 196 AK-47 live rounds of ammunition and N675,000 in cash, among other operations. The activities included WADA enlightenment lectures for students and staff of Poko Community Primary School, Poka, Epe, Lagos; Community Grammar School, Eyinni, Ibadan, Oyo State; and Iganmode Grammar School, Ota, Ogun State, among others. The Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the NDLEA, Brig-Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.), lauded the operatives for their vigilance and professionalism, noting that the “interception of methamphetamine concealed in breakfast cereals shows that no concealment method, however ingenious, can beat the resolve of the agency’s operatives.” Kindly share this story:
